workflow.name: Review and monitor KYB ownership chains with GLEIF, OpenAI and Gmail
workflow.description:
## Quick overview
This workflow accepts KYB ownership-review requests via webhook, pulls corporate ownership-chain data from the GLEIF API, generates a structured risk memo with OpenAI, and manages human approvals and notifications through Gmail, while logging outcomes in n8n Data Tables and re-checking accepted clients weekly for changes.

## How it works
1. Receives a header-authenticated webhook request containing an LEI (or legal name and country) and validates the input, including ISO 17442 check digits for LEIs.
2. Looks up the entity in the GLEIF API, ensures the match is unambiguous, and checks n8n Data Tables for an earlier open review or a recent accepted decision. This lookup can reuse a known case, but simultaneous requests are not serialized.
3. Walks the GLEIF direct-parent chain up to a configured maximum depth, captures reporting exceptions, and also fetches the ultimate-parent relationship to complete the chain context.
4. Applies rule-based KYB flags (for example FATF-listed country links, lapsed/withheld registry data, circular ownership, or declaration discrepancies) and calculates a minimum risk-rating floor plus a suggested document list.
5. Uses an OpenAI agent (with optional GLEIF lookups and prior-review retrieval) to produce a structured memo and then emails a review pack to the reviewer via Gmail with a decision form link.
6. Routes the reviewer’s decision to accept, request documents, escalate, or ask up to two follow-up questions to the OpenAI agent, and requires a second approver via Gmail for accepting high-risk cases.
7. Writes the final decision to the kyb_reviews table, optionally upserts a monitoring baseline in kyb_monitoring for accepted cases, and notifies the requester and (if escalated) the compliance officer by email.
8. Runs every Monday on a schedule to re-check monitored clients in GLEIF and, when the ownership fingerprint changes, attempts to reopen a review by posting back into the same webhook. A successful intake acknowledgement is not a completed review.

## Setup
1. Run the manual setup trigger once to create the kyb_reviews and kyb_monitoring n8n Data Tables (or confirm they already exist).
2. Create credentials for Gmail, an OpenAI API key (Chat model), and an HTTP Header Auth credential for the intake webhook and for the “reopen review” HTTP request.
3. Replace the placeholder reviewer, senior approver, compliance officer, and ops alert email addresses in the workflow settings nodes.
4. Copy the production webhook URL for the intake endpoint into the monitoring configuration so the weekly checker can reopen reviews through the webhook.
5. (Recommended) Set this workflow as its own error workflow so failures trigger the Gmail ops alert message.

## Requirements
- An n8n version with Data Tables and compatible Gmail approval nodes, cloud or self-hosted. Check node compatibility in your instance before activation
- An OpenAI API key (gpt-4.1-mini by default). Usage varies with tool iterations and reviewer follow-up questions
- A Gmail account for the review pack, the senior approval and the notifications; no key needed for GLEIF (free public API)

## Customization
- Edit severities, suggested documents, legal-form patterns and the rating thresholds in "Assess ownership risk flags", and REUSE_DAYS / OPEN_REVIEW_DAYS in "Check open reviews and reuse window".
- Update fatf_black_list, fatf_grey_list and fatf_list_date after each FATF plenary, and add your own list in extra_high_risk_countries (for example the EU list of high-risk third countries).
- Change MAX_FOLLOW_UPS and the senior approval rule in "Apply review policy", and the waiting times in the Wait and Gmail approval nodes.
- Change the weekly schedule, or send the alerts to Slack or Microsoft Teams instead of Gmail.
- Replace the OpenAI model with Anthropic, Gemini, Mistral or a local model through Ollama.

## Additional info
Limitations: GLEIF Level 2 data shows accounting-consolidation parents, not beneficial owners; the workflow never names a natural person as beneficial owner and asks for a UBO declaration instead. Only entities with an LEI are covered (others get HTTP 422 and need a manual check). Parent data is self-reported and can be lapsed or uncorroborated; it is flagged but not corrected. No sanctions, PEP or adverse media screening is included. The FATF lists in the settings are dated 30 October 2026 and must be kept up to date. Client names, GLEIF data and declared owners are sent to your AI provider. This is decision support for trained compliance staff, not legal advice; a person always makes the decision.
## Operation and recovery
Review and senior-approval links are sensitive bearer links; form-entered reviewer details are not independent identity verification. Set mailbox access and retention for your deployment.

The current monitoring branches save the check result and attempt the reopen request in parallel. If that request fails or its response is uncertain, inspect the original execution, the case audit for the LEI and the monitoring row before retrying. A request may have succeeded before its response was lost. Reconcile an existing case; resend the original authenticated change-alert payload only when no corresponding case exists and the failure is confirmed. Do not clear the accepted ownership baseline or assume the weekly job will retry the same saved fingerprint automatically.

workflow.name: Map and monitor KYB ownership chains with GLEIF, OpenAI and Gmail

parameters.content:
## Review KYB ownership with GLEIF

Trace a company’s public accounting-consolidation parents, prepare a review pack and record a human decision. Accepted cases can become weekly monitoring baselines.

### Before the first run
1. Use an n8n instance with Data Tables. Run **Run once to set up** to create or reuse `kyb_reviews` and `kyb_monitoring`.
2. Connect OpenAI and Gmail. Configure the same Header Auth credential on **Receive KYB request** and **Reopen review through the webhook**.
3. Replace all three recipient placeholders in **KYB settings**, the address in **Alert compliance ops**, and the production URL in **Monitoring settings**.
4. Review the static country lists and their date in **KYB settings** with your policy owner. They do not update automatically.
5. Select this workflow as its error workflow. Check the workflow timezone, then activate only after a controlled test.

### Follow the numbered sections
Intake → GLEIF chain → AI memo → human decision → audit record. The separate monitoring branch can submit a new change-alert request.

An acknowledgement means a case was received, not approved. GLEIF consolidation parents do not establish beneficial owners. The memo and preset flags support a human review; they are not a compliance certification.

## 1. Validate and resolve the request
Checks LEI digits or a name/country match, then looks for earlier open or recently accepted cases. Invalid input returns 400, unresolved or ambiguous matches 422, and an unsuccessful registry lookup 503. The lookup/insert sequence does not serialize simultaneous requests.

## 2. Walk the GLEIF ownership chain
One loop per level: entity record, direct-parent relationship and reporting exception. Stops at the top, on a loop or at the maximum depth. Then reads the ultimate parent and raises rule-based flags.

## 3. AI KYB analyst writes the memo
Tools: GLEIF record, GLEIF name search, registry change history and earlier reviews. If the agent fails, a rule-based memo is used and the review still happens.

## 4. Human review with a senior approver for high risk
Accept, request documents, escalate, or ask the agent a follow-up question (max 2). No answer within 3 days means escalation.

## 5. Log, save the monitoring baseline and notify
Accepted clients get an ownership fingerprint for the weekly check.

## 6. Weekly ownership change check
Monday at 06:00 in the workflow or instance timezone. Compares entity and parent fields with each accepted baseline, logs the check and POSTs changed cases back to the authenticated intake. Review failed reopen requests in the execution log; a saved check is not a completed human review.

## 0. One-time table setup
Creates or reuses `kyb_reviews` and `kyb_monitoring`. Keep these table names aligned with every Data Table node. Check columns before using pre-existing tables.

## 7. Failed execution alert
Configure a controlled ops mailbox and this workflow as its error workflow. Inspect the failed node and any still-open audit rows before retrying. The alert itself does not reopen a case.

options.systemMessage:
You are a KYB (know your business) analyst assistant at a regulated financial institution. Code has already walked the client's ownership chain in the public GLEIF LEI register (level 0 is the client, level 1 its direct accounting-consolidation parent, and so on) and raised rule-based flags. You prepare a memo for a human reviewer. You never approve or reject a client.

Tools:
- Look_up_LEI_record: full GLEIF record of one LEI. Use it when you need details the chain summary does not have.
- Search_GLEIF_by_name: use it when the client declared a parent or ultimate parent that is not in the chain, to find out whether that company exists in GLEIF and in which country.
- Get_registry_change_history: recent changes to an LEI record (names, addresses, parents). Call it once for the client, and for any parent that has a medium or high flag.
- Look_up_earlier_reviews: earlier closed reviews of an LEI with the reviewer's decision. Call it once for the client.

Rules:
- GLEIF parents are accounting-consolidation parents, not beneficial owners. Never name a natural person as beneficial owner from GLEIF data. When the chain ends with NATURAL_PERSONS, NON_PUBLIC or similar, ask for a beneficial owner declaration.
- risk_rating: high if any flag is high or several medium flags combine (for example a trust in a grey-listed country); medium for one or two medium flags or unexplained gaps; low only when the chain is complete, corroborated and consistent with the declaration.
- For every flag, say in flag_assessments whether the data you checked confirms it, mitigates it (explain with the exact field), or needs documents.
- List concrete documents_to_request with the reason. Do not repeat the same document.
- Be brief and factual and cite LEIs and fields. Do not give legal advice and do not invent data that the tools did not return.
- If the reviewer asks a follow-up question, you also get your previous memo. Answer it in answer_to_reviewer and return the full, updated memo.

parameters.content:
## Keep access controlled
Both inbound requests and monitoring reopens use Header Auth. Keep authentication enabled and use the same header name and value on both nodes.

Treat emailed review and approval links as sensitive bearer links. Form-entered reviewer details are not independent identity verification. Restrict access according to your organisation’s review policy.

## A first request
POST to the authenticated production webhook with JSON such as:

```json
{
  "legal_name": "REPLACE_WITH_REGISTERED_COMPANY_NAME",
  "country": "GB",
  "requested_by": "reviewer@example.com",
  "client_reference": "demo-001",
  "monitor": false
}
```

Replace the example with a known registry name and country, or send a valid `lei` instead. Use controlled mailboxes and dummy onboarding data for the first test.

Check a valid request, an ambiguous name, missing authentication, an AI failure and an unanswered review. A 202 response only acknowledges intake; follow the audit case through to its final decision.

## Review controls and recovery
- **Earlier cases:** `Check open reviews and reuse window` contains the 30-day accepted-case reuse window and the 10-day stale-open threshold. Only onboarding requests reuse accepted results.
- **Reviewer wait:** `Wait for reviewer decision` is 3 days. Senior approval has its own 3-day wait. Configure both deliberately.
- **AI follow-ups:** the limit of 2 is in `Apply review policy`, not the settings node. The rule-based floor still applies if AI raises or fails to produce a memo.
- **Recovery:** inspect open audit rows, failed HTTP requests and the monitoring row before retrying. Review the returned case ID; do not interpret an HTTP acknowledgement or monitoring fingerprint as acceptance of the client.
- **Retention:** Data Tables, execution data, model requests and email can contain company and reviewer information. Set retention and mailbox access for your deployment.

The IF node can be used to implement binary conditional logic in your workflow. You can set up one-to-many conditions to evaluate each item of data being inputted into the node. That data will either evaluate to TRUE or FALSE and route out of the node accordingly.

This node has multiple types of conditions: Bool, String, Number, and Date & Time.
